title: A chart or title keeps what you set by hand when you change its numbers or style
goal: Changing an animated chart's numbers or theme lays its bars out again and throws away any key or effect the person set by hand on a bar, and restyling a chart or title puts back the theme's version of an effect the person had edited. The person loses work without being told. Keep hand-set keys and edited effects through a change of numbers or style, the way hand-dragged title bars are now kept.
notes: From two audit rough lines nobody filed: queue/audits/2026-10-17-animated-charts.json ('Changing the data or the theme lays the chart's pieces out again: a key or an effect set by hand on one bar is lost (the pieces keep their ids, and a part's retimed in and out are kept)') and queue/audits/2026-10-19-a-title-part-move-dragged-by-hand-on-the-timelin.json ('On a chart, an effect the drawing gave a bar and that you then edited (rather than added) still goes back to the theme's on a restyle; only effects you added are kept'). The model to copy is commit 56d7c8e5 (hand-dragged title part bars survive a restyle). Not reproduced by the manager, so p2 with reproduction as the first item.
acceptance: Reproduced first at Next defaults: drop a Bar chart on a video, key one bar's opacity by hand and edit its shadow, then change one number, then the theme; what was lost goes in this task's log

After a change of numbers or theme, a key set by hand on a bar stays on that bar, and an effect the person edited keeps their values; a bar that goes away (its row removed) takes its own keys with it and nothing else
The same on a title: an effect the person edited, not only one they added, survives a theme, font pair or energy change
A walk at Next defaults proves both and joins the rotating set; unit tests in PhotonzCore for the merge; Scripts/test.sh passes
Audit written under queue/audits/. Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: note from a-chart-is-your-data-given-to-it-the-obvious-way: a chart with later sets is now posed at every frame from the numbers of that moment (ChartData.swift, ChartPen.posed); the pose keeps each piece's own style, keys and text settings and only changes place, size, shape and words, so hand-set looks survive there. Stored pieces are still laid out by ChartPen.rebuilt as before.
